system.summary: Two-digit homophonic cipher with nulls 2 and 5 and three-digit nomenclator codes followed by a null digit, used for short passages in clear Italian.
system.sibling_key: DECODE DOC D3246/D3247 on R60/R61: Biermann-Bosbach reconstructed key for ASV F64 1625, transcribed by Lasry
system.notes: R61 also has one line of letter-sign cipher, not in this key, not attacked.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the leaves; key reconstructed by Biermann and Bosbach, on DECODE since 2020

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: decode_with_key.py (DP segmentation over the key with gap penalty)

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record pages, six images and the two DOC_ files with the session cookie.
DOC_ files on both records hold the Biermann-Bosbach 1625 key (Lasry transcription).
Read the pages: R60 Spada 15 Aug 1625 and R61 Naro last Feb 1625, each with an interlinear decipherment over the figures.
Transcribed the R60 and R61 figure runs from zoomed crops.
Decoded with the key: R60 'a fratelo del arcivescovo', 'gnor' under 'Monsignore'; R61 ends 'di loro natura', matching the glosses.
R59 (catalogue 255): three glossed passages decoded with the same key: 'generale de le galere', 'l'ambasciar...', '...contraria'.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions r59/r60/r61_digits.txt; the interlinear decipherments copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/R59-R61_decryption.md; R60's gloss is transcribed only in part (rest on the image) and R61's letter-sign line is untranscribed.

v3 verification: R59 scored as Latin on its decryption file with figure strings (0.5). The three glossed passages written out in texts/R59_reading.md (Italian): 1.0 explicit-hole and plain. Language set to it; keeps read.

Verification 5 (plain-bar rows): R60 and R61 were listed as Spanish/French and scored on copied NOTES paragraphs. Both are Italian. DECODE images IMG_R60_I463_P3 and IMG_R61_I464_P1 fetched with the project cookie: R60's two glossed cipher runs read in full (the '…' were clear text); R61's foot decipherment is tied by its + to the letter-sign line, whose word division agrees. Readings texts/R60_reading.md (plain 0.6, explicit 0.8) and texts/R61_reading.md (plain 0.667, explicit 1.0). Keep read.

outcome.method_basis: All three letters (R59-R61) carry the Roman office's interlinear decipherment over the cipher runs; the Biermann-Bosbach key already on the DECODE records (Lasry's transcription) was applied to confirm stretches.
outcome.notes: Read at the time; key confirmed on stretches. R61 letter-sign line not attacked.

texts.label: R59, Naro, Paris 14 Apr 1625
texts.summary: Bernardino Naro, Paris 14 April 1625, to the Secretariat of State: Richelieu, the Aldobrandini precedent and lodging for the coming legate; the three cipher passages (the General of the galleys, procuring the ordinary embassy at Rome, the Cardinal of Lyon will oppose it) carry the contemporary decipherment above them.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored texts/R59_decryption.md as Latin (no language on the entry; 0.5 explicit-hole on 74 words of header and figure strings), a false alarm. The three passages are Italian and carry their contemporary decipherment, checked against the Biermann-Bosbach key; written out in texts/R59_reading.md: 1.0 explicit-hole and plain (3/3). Short runs inside a clear letter whose clear text is not transcribed.

texts.label: R60, Spada, Paris 15 Aug 1625
texts.summary: The nuncio Bernardino Spada, archbishop of Damiata, Paris 15 August 1625: clear Italian news (Fontainebleau, Richelieu, Mansfeld's officer, the English fleet, Vaudémont, Verdun) with three short cipher runs on f. 138r about a copy of a letter shown by the brother of an archbishop.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026: listed as Spanish; the letter is Italian (1625), so the plain share is a bar too. The sweep scored texts/R60_decryption.md (copied NOTES paragraph with '…' gaps and key strings: plain 0.0, explicit 0.714). The DECODE image IMG_R60_I463_P3 (f. 138r) was fetched and read: the '…' were only the clear words of the letter; the two cipher runs are glossed 'Il fratello dell'Arcivescovo' + 'di Livorni' and 'Monsignore'. Reading texts/R60_reading.md (glosses with the clear sentence around them): plain 0.6 (3/5), explicit 0.8 (4/5); the see 'di Livorni' marked doubtful. Keeps read.

texts.label: R61, Naro, Paris 28 Feb 1625
texts.summary: Bernardino Naro, Paris, last day of February 1625, with a copy of a Brussels letter of 21 Feb 1625 (Mirabello, the Savoy ambassador); two lines of figures, deciphered above, on the French being very suspicious and jealous by nature.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026: listed as French; the letter is Italian (1625). The sweep scored texts/R61_decryption.md (copied NOTES paragraph: plain 0.167, explicit 1.0). On the DECODE image IMG_R61_I464_P1 (f. 186r) the decipherment at the foot carries the same + as the letter-sign line after 'prudentemente', and the word division of that line agrees with it, so the decipherment reads the + line (the figures under it decode in part, their end '... di loro natura'). Reading texts/R61_reading.md, the decipherment set in its clear sentence: plain 0.667 (2/3), explicit 1.0 (3/3). Keeps read; the old note (letter-sign line unread) is withdrawn.
